documents.title: Artificial Intelligence at Portland State University
documents.summary: The Academic Affairs page sets out six AI principles (human-centered, equity, literacy, academic freedom, transparency, shared integrity) and links to guidance for students, faculty and researchers. It welcomes AI, leaves course rules to instructors, and lists university-provided tools and support.
documents.stance_why: The page says "Expectations for the acceptable use of AI in a course are determined by the instructor and may differ from class to class" and gives faculty "the autonomy to determine if and how AI tools are integrated"; it sets no default for students, so it delegates.

units.why: The opening sentence states the institution's position that it "embraces responsible use" of AI as a tool for teaching, learning and research; this is a framework preamble (P56), and the welcome gives it an encouraging stance.
units.anchor: embraces responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI) as a transformative tool
units.frag_start: Portland State University’s AI Working Group embraces
units.fit_note: Also welcomes AI use as a default attitude (P02), but sets no operational rule.

units.why: "We prioritize 'Human-in-the-Loop' practices where critical evaluations, final decisions, and ethical judgments are made by people, not algorithms" bars AI from being the decision-maker, so it belongs with human responsibility for decisions (P73).
units.anchor: final decisions, and ethical judgments are made by people, not algorithms

units.why: "does not widen the digital divide" and "equitable access to tools" is an access and equity commitment, matching P51.
units.anchor: ensuring that AI adoption does not widen the digital divide
units.fit_note: A university commitment to equitable access, not a rule that paid tools are not required.

units.why: "We strive to provide equitable access to tools and critically evaluate AI systems for biases" names bias evaluation as a university aim, so it is a bias/harms statement (P53).
units.anchor: critically evaluate AI systems for biases

units.why: "PSU is committed to fostering AI literacy across the institution" commits the university to AI-literacy education for students, faculty and staff (P70).
units.anchor: PSU is committed to fostering AI literacy across the institution

units.why: "faculty have the autonomy to determine if and how AI tools are integrated into their teaching" leaves the AI decision to each instructor (P04), not to a university rule.
units.anchor: faculty have the autonomy to determine if and how AI tools are integrated

units.why: "a culture of experimentation and exploration ... rather than one of restriction" sets a default welcoming attitude toward AI, matching P02.
units.anchor: a culture of experimentation and exploration of ways AI can improve learning
units.frag_start: We encourage a culture of experimentation

units.why: "We expect transparency ... This includes acknowledging AI's role in the generative process" expects AI use to be acknowledged, which is disclosure (P24).
units.anchor: acknowledging AI's role in the generative process
units.fit_note: Principle for the whole community, not a per-submission requirement.

units.why: "being forthcoming about how these tools are utilized in administrative decision-making" addresses AI in university operations, so P76 rather than P24, which concerns coursework.
units.anchor: being forthcoming about how these tools are utilized in administrative decision-making

units.why: "the individual remains accountable for the accuracy, attribution, and ethical impact of their output" makes the person responsible for AI-assisted output, matching P29.
units.anchor: the individual remains accountable for the accuracy, attribution, and ethical impact of their output
units.frag_start: While AI may assist in the process

units.why: "Expectations for the acceptable use of AI in a course are determined by the instructor and may differ from class to class" is the university delegating the rule to instructors (P04).
units.anchor: Expectations for the acceptable use of AI in a course are determined by the instructor

units.why: "Students should check with their instructors and read the syllabi" tells students where to learn what is allowed; P10 (ask first) fits better than P09 because it is addressed to students.
units.anchor: Students should check with their instructors and read the syllabi

units.why: The page says the university "understands that artificial intelligence (AI) brings both opportunities and risks to student learning," a framing statement that gives no rule.
units.anchor: brings both opportunities and risks to student learning
units.frag_end: opportunities and risks to student learning.
units.fit_note: Framing statement with no rule; the nearest type is the framework preamble.

units.why: The Library "offers guidance on citation styles for generative AI, helping students avoid plagiarism and credit sources accurately" points to a citation resource, supporting attribution of AI use (P24).
units.anchor: The PSU Library offers guidance on citation styles for generative AI
units.fit_note: A pointer to citation guidance, not a requirement to cite.

units.why: "guidance on protecting personal data when using AI applications like ChatGPT, Copilot" is a data privacy resource for students (P50).
units.anchor: guidance on protecting personal data when using AI applications

units.why: "offers AI teaching resources and support consultations to all educators" is faculty support for AI, matching P63.
units.anchor: offers AI teaching resources and support consultations to all educators at PSU

units.why: The AI Syllabus Language resource says "Setting clear expectations on AI usage is essential" and offers sample language, which supports syllabus statements (P09).
units.anchor: Setting clear expectations on AI usage is essential
units.fit_note: Offers sample language and says expectations are essential; does not require a syllabus statement.

units.why: "PSU provides faculty, staff, and students with access to a suite of generative AI tools, including Google's Gemini and NotebookLM" is a sanctioned, university-provided AI tool (P17).
units.anchor: PSU provides faculty, staff, and students with access to a suite of generative AI tools

units.why: "When using or procuring AI tools, please be sure to follow PSU's guidelines and policies" ties tool use to existing university policy (P77).
units.anchor: please be sure to follow PSU’s guidelines and policies
units.frag_start: When using or procuring AI tools,

units.why: "Faculty and students involved in research ... are encouraged to explore AI's potential while adhering to ethical standards" is a rule for research use (P62).
units.anchor: are encouraged to explore AI’s potential while adhering to ethical standards
units.frag_start: Faculty and students involved in research

units.why: The Teaching guide is described as having "regular updates to keep pace with AI advancements," which is a commitment to revising guidance (P54).
units.anchor: with regular updates to keep pace with AI advancements

units.why: The Working Group "is tasked with recommending AI guidance and tools" for the community, describing who maintains the guidance (governance).
units.anchor: tasked with recommending AI guidance and tools
units.fit_note: Describes who maintains AI guidance; closest type is the institutional framework.

documents.title: Academic Misconduct (incl. 'Academic Misconduct and AI')
documents.summary: The Dean of Student Life page explains how the Student Code applies to AI: unauthorized AI is misconduct, authorized AI must be used as specified and cited. It gives faculty advice on syllabus statements, assignment design, detectors and reporting, and lists student rights in conduct review.
documents.stance_why: The page says AI use "without prior explicit authorization from the instructor assigning the work, would be considered a potential violation of the code," so AI is barred unless an instructor permits it.

units.why: "submitted ... is their own original work, completed without the use of unauthorized materials and tools" sets the baseline that submitted work must be the student's own (P29).
units.anchor: work students submit is their own original work, completed without the use of unauthorized materials
units.frag_start: At PSU, the expectation under our

units.why: "While the code doesn't explicitly prohibit AI technology, it does prohibit cheating, the use of unauthorized materials ... which would include tools like AI generators" classifies unauthorized AI as misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: which would include tools like AI generators

units.why: "the use of AI ... without prior explicit authorization from the instructor ... would be considered a potential violation" makes AI banned unless authorized, a fallback/default rule (P06); the referral clause is a consequence within the same sentence.
units.anchor: without prior explicit authorization from the instructor assigning the work
units.frag_start: Please know, the use of AI
units.fit_note: Also says violations are referred to the Director of Student Conduct and Conflict Resolution.

units.why: "you would need to properly cite the sources of that work" requires attribution of AI-generated material that is not the student's own (P24).
units.anchor: you would need to properly cite the sources of that work
units.frag_start: If you do use materials and

units.why: "When an instructor does permit the use of AI programs ... they should be used as specified in the assignment instructions" ties permitted use to each assignment (P04).
units.anchor: they should be used as specified in the assignment instructions
units.frag_start: When an instructor does permit the

units.why: "check with your instructor, use the library, or reach out to the Writing Center" directs students to human help when unsure; P72 fits better than P10 because it names library and Writing Center.
units.anchor: check with your instructor, use the library, or reach out to the
units.frag_start: If you have questions about the use

units.why: "students should be cautious about the use of AI for academic work" discourages AI use without banning it (P03).
units.anchor: students should be cautious about the use of AI for academic work

units.why: "If you choose not to allow AI programs, be clear about this in the syllabus" asks instructors to state their AI rule in the syllabus (P09).
units.anchor: be clear about this in the syllabus
units.frag_start: If you choose not to allow
units.frag_end: at the start of the term.

units.why: "discuss it at the start of the term" asks instructors to talk through the rule with students, which is explaining the rules (P66) rather than only writing them down (P09).
units.anchor: discuss it at the start of the term
units.frag_start: If you choose not to allow
units.frag_end: at the start of the term.

units.why: "If you choose to allow AI programs ... clarify the expectations around the proper use, limitations on assignments, and any pitfalls" asks instructors who permit AI to spell out the terms (P09).
units.anchor: clarify the expectations around the proper use, limitations on assignments, and any pitfalls
units.frag_start: If you choose to allow AI programs,

units.why: "Talk with students about both the potential and pitfalls in AI generators" recommends instructors discuss AI with students, matching P66.
units.anchor: Talk with students about both the potential and pitfalls in AI generators

units.why: "consider updating assignment structures and prompts to avoid them being easily solved/written by AI" recommends redesigning assignments around AI (P35).
units.anchor: updating assignment structures and prompts to avoid them being easily solved/written by AI

units.why: "Become familiar with a few AI generators ... to identify AI generated work" advises instructors to learn the tools, matching P63.
units.anchor: Become familiar with a few AI generators
units.fit_note: Purpose is to recognize AI-generated student work.

units.why: "Do not rely entirely on these programs to determine the use of AI" says detectors are inaccurate and cannot be sole proof (P39).
units.anchor: Do not rely entirely on these programs to determine the use of AI

units.why: "The student should be made aware of the situation ... outline how you came to the conclusion" tells instructors to speak with the student before the process continues (P57).
units.anchor: The student should be made aware of the situation.
units.frag_end: what your next steps will be.
units.fit_note: Applies to academic dishonesty generally, which includes AI.

units.why: "Give a proper grade ... In most cases, this will be a '0' or 'F'" states a concrete penalty (P37).
units.anchor: In most cases, this will be a "0" or "F”
units.frag_start: Give a proper grade for the
units.fit_note: General academic dishonesty rule, not AI-specific; grade is at instructor discretion.

units.why: "instructors may not grade beyond the specific assignment or exam in question" caps the penalty an instructor may apply (P37).
units.anchor: instructors may not grade beyond the specific assignment or exam in question
units.fit_note: Limits instructor penalties rather than stating one.

units.why: "It is recommended that you have a consistent practice in grading ... outlined in your syllabus" asks instructors to publish their sanctions in advance (P37).
units.anchor: have a consistent practice in grading as a result of academic misconduct
units.frag_start: It is recommended that you have
units.frag_end: outlined in your syllabus for the course.

units.why: "Report the matter to the Conduct Office" routes suspected dishonesty to the integrity process (P36).
units.anchor: Report the matter to the Conduct Office.
units.frag_end: Any documentation you can provide is helpful.

units.why: "you have the opportunity to participate in the review process, share your perspective" gives accused students a right to respond (P64).
units.anchor: you have the opportunity to participate in the review process, share your perspective
units.frag_start: If you have received an email

units.why: The student is given "Notice of the report, allegations, and which sections of the Code are alleged to be violated" as a fairness safeguard (P64).
units.anchor: Notice of the report, allegations, and which sections of the Code
units.fit_note: Procedural fairness for conduct cases generally.

units.why: "Opportunity to appeal the outcome" is a safeguard for accused students (P64).
units.anchor: Opportunity to appeal the outcome

units.fit_note: Procedural fairness for conduct cases generally.

documents.title: CS Graduate Student Handbook 2025-26 (section 11.8)
documents.summary: Section 11.8 of the CS Graduate Student Handbook says the department follows the university academic-misconduct rules. It adds that generative-AI rules differ by course, so students should read each syllabus.
documents.stance_why: The single AI sentence says "the use of generative AI may differ widely among CS courses" and tells students to "consult the course syllabus," with no department rule of its own.

units.why: "The CS department follows the university's general rules on academic misconduct" adopts the university rules for the department (P77).
units.anchor: The CS department follows the university’s general rules on academic misconduct

units.why: "the particular rules for independent work and the use of generative AI may differ widely among CS courses" says each course sets its own rules, so P11, and tells students to read each syllabus.
units.anchor: the use of generative AI may differ widely among CS courses
units.fit_note: Also tells students to consult the syllabus (P10).

notes: Coder A. Course syllabi deferred in collect file. The AI page links to PSU guideline pages (ethical use, syllabus language, teaching guide) that were not in the saved text; only the page text was coded. The Dean of Student Life page contains general misconduct procedures, so only AI-relevant passages and faculty recommendations were coded; the CS handbook has one AI sentence.
